text: Not long after, frost creeps across the rooftop room from the bed, where Jaeha sits rigid, eyes glowing cyan, nose bleeding.
Seoa tries to shake him awake. Nib catches her wrist: wherever Jaeha is, it isn't this room.
Frost forms on his lashes.
In front of him, a small window counts down. Twenty-two seconds left, and nobody has said yes.
Rewind ten minutes. The room is warm and ordinary, Gomi is squashed against the window, and Jaeha is writing fast.
He's drafting his offer to the Far Side, laid out like every job posting he ever answered, ramen doodle included.
Seoa reads it over his shoulder with flat eyes. Jaeha is very proud of it.
Nib knows the Far Side better than anyone here, and he doesn't think much of the pay.
Then, without looking, he yanks the curtain shut on Gomi's squashed face.
Jaeha isn't convinced. Four years of guilds taught him one law of business.
So he asks what he has wondered since the boss room. Nib's reason had nothing to do with money.
Seoa raises a practical concern about the size of the room. Jaeha has a practical answer.
Seoa crouches with her stopwatch and won't let him go without his word. He tells her it's nothing dangerous.
Then he presses the glowing button.
And he's standing on endless black water under a starless sky, ringed by tall glowing rifts. One minute.
He turns slowly, taking them in.
Every rift is a door to a different world. A fortress burns under a great bell, and in a green field, a long hill seems to breathe.
Through one, a tall archer stands on a riverbank, a long beaded braid over her shoulder.
Through another, a broad figure in surgeon's plate bends over a bed.
The system tells him to make his offer. Jaeha clears his throat like a best man before a speech.
Then he reads the advert to the whole Far Side, word for word, ramen and all.
It goes badly. The archer turns her back, something in the forest walks away, and the whispers aren't kind.
Then the burning fortress flares. Beside a swinging bell, a broad figure in bell-shaped armour turns toward him. Fifty-two seconds.
Finally, someone speaks to him. Jaeha's face lights up, but the voice from the wall isn't impressed either.
Jaeha steps forward anyway, sure he can close the deal.
The figure strikes its bell, and a ring of light hurls the swarm back from its wall. It isn't refusing forever. Its wall just hasn't fallen yet.
The rift closes like an eye, and its line to Jaeha snaps. Forty-one seconds left.
The hope drains from Jaeha's face, his hand still reaching for a door already shut.
So he does what desperate salesmen do and raises the price. Two more rifts go grey.
In the room, Nib goes rigid at a faint ringing in the air. He heard that bell once, the day it rang the retreat.
One by one, the rifts go dark. Thirty-five seconds.
So he does what a trap-tester always does with a contract. He scrolls to the bottom.
The fine print: they hear what he means, not what he says. He can still change his offer, but if nobody accepts, Route Alignment resets.
And Jaeha realises what they heard. Not a promise. A sales pitch.
Then he remembers why Nib came. It was never about the pay.
Then the still water trembles, and something dark rises beneath his feet. Twenty-eight seconds.
A black hand with too many joints clamps round his ankle, frost racing up his leg.
The window tears into red and blue static. Something unregistered is listening, and one line names another Operator, number one, hushed.
In the room, frost bursts from his right foot. Whatever has him there has him here too.
Outside the window, Gomi arches her back and hisses at the glow.
The hand drags him down to the knees, his reflection breaking apart around him. Twenty seconds.
He tears the job advert out of his notebook.
And lets it sink.
He stops fighting, straightens up, and faces the dark rifts with nothing to read from. This time he starts with the truth.
Then he offers what he gave Nib: his own body between them and the worst of it.
Last, the one rule he gave Nib on the night they met.
In the room, Nib's notched ear lifts as if he heard that, and his mouth almost smiles.
The last few lines flicker brighter. The new offer is in, with twelve seconds to spare.
Ten seconds. Jaeha closes his eyes.
Seven. The rifts stay dark, and the hand drags him to his waist.
In the room, Seoa holds his frost-white hand against her forehead.
Five. He's chest-deep, his breath fogging, still watching the rifts.
Four seconds of darkness.
Three. Then the mossy rift glows, and the long, flowered hill rises as if breathing. Something like a shoulder lifts.
And in the moss, two huge, slow amber eyes begin to open.
